A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Ctrl-Z Sampling work. Text, equations, algorithms, tables and figures are readable throughout. v1 has no separate appendix; v2 includes readable supplementary material on PDF pages 11–16.

before.justification: v1 reports original Stable Diffusion 2.1 experiments on Pick-a-Pic and DrawBench, including baseline comparisons, ablations and generated-image examples.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments with Stable Diffusion 2.1 and Hunyuan-DiT, adds T2I-CompBench results, and includes additional quantitative ablations and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: The core reward-guided inversion sampler remains. Algorithm 1 changes the exploration condition from t ≤ T−λ to t ≥ T−λ, aligning it with the early-exploration prose already present in v1. It also moves the stopping test outside the N-candidate loop. These are localized revisions to the reported procedure.

E1.justification: Pick-a-Pic and DrawBench are retained. v2 adds systematic compositional evaluation on T2I-CompBench, reporting color, shape, texture, spatial-relation and numeracy results in Tables 2 and 4. This substantially extends the evaluated prompt population and explicit compositional requirements.

E2.justification: The main comparator set remains DDIM, Resampling, Z-Sampling and SOP; Resample is renamed Resampling. Within the reward-model comparison, v2 Table 3 adds a CLIPScore-guided variant to the HPSv2, AES, PickScore and ImageReward variants evaluated in v1 Table 2.

E3.justification: Reported main settings change from λ=15, N=20, unrestricted depth and δ=0.01 to λ=40, N=4, maximum depth 3 and δ=0; SOP candidates change from 5 to 4. v2 adds Hunyuan-DiT evaluation, compositional category scores and approximately compute-matched controls. These changes prevent treating revised scores as same-setting gains. Figure 4's exact threshold sweep is ambiguous because its caption and legend disagree.

E4.justification: v2 adds depth-versus-width analysis in Figure 2, approximately compute-matched Always-explore comparisons in Table 5, exploration-probability sweeps in Table 6 and exploration-window sensitivity in Table 7. It expands reward-model testing and qualitative cases. The existing threshold/depth analysis is retained in revised supplementary Figure 4, rather than removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Increased search candidates and additional result rows do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Numerous results are replaced or added under revised settings. For example, Ctrl-Z's SD2.1 ImageReward scores change from 0.776 to 1.138 on Pick-a-Pic and from 0.685 to 1.025 on DrawBench. SOP now exceeds Ctrl-Z on SD2.1 PickScore in both benchmarks, reversing v1's ordering. Hunyuan-DiT, CompBench and additional ablation results substantially expand the evidence. HPS rescaling and equivalent rounding are excluded from this judgment.

T1.justification: The substantive DDIM, clean-image estimation, inversion and reward-threshold mathematics in Equations 1–6 is retained. Noise-schedule and index notation is cleaned up, but no new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The central claims of model-agnostic, reward-guided escape from local optima and improved conditional generation remain. v2 makes the efficiency advantage of fewer, deeper searches an explicit experimental contribution and revises the abstract's stated NFE increase from approximately 7.6× to 6.72×.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations and limitations concerning high-reward plateaus, fixed-threshold instability, late-stage reward overfitting and diminishing returns. It discusses the Hunyuan-DiT numeracy exception and hypothesizes mechanisms behind spatial-relation results. The supplement explicitly limits conclusions about large-scale inference because of resource constraints, extending v1's more general quality–efficiency discussion.

D1.justification: v1 already documents core hyperparameters and an RTX 3090. v2 adds image resolutions, CPU specifications, a second RTX 4090 setup, Ubuntu and CUDA versions, and PyTorch 2.4.0/Diffusers 0.32.2. It also documents revised configurations and expands baseline descriptions. These refine reproducibility information; no code or data release instructions are added.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for T2I-CompBench, Hunyuan-DiT and Choi et al.'s Fair Sampling through Switching Mechanism. The overall positioning against fixed-depth exploration and other inference-time techniques remains. Bibliographic formatting changes do not represent additional research-positioning changes.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites and consolidates related work, revises method explanations, compresses the main experimental-settings section and moves expanded settings into the supplement. The ablation narrative is reorganized around depth versus width, with threshold analysis moved to supplementary material and new interpretation and limitations sections added.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn using layered two-dimensional landscapes. Tables gain model groupings, NFE columns and revised highlighting, alongside new benchmark and ablation tables. The threshold plot is relocated and redrawn, and qualitative displays gain changed examples, colored borders and an additional image grid.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence that was limited to one architecture and two benchmarks: Hunyuan-DiT and compositional evaluations test generality, while depth-versus-width and approximately compute-matched ablations directly examine the claimed exploration advantage. Added implementation details and substantive failure conditions improve assessability. Figure 4's conflicting labels and Algorithm 1's unclear stopping check remain weaknesses, but the broader, more diagnostic validation provides a substantial net quality improvement.
